pages.body:
This is a picture blog. Each post is one picture, a title and a date; some carry
a caption or a line or two about how the thing was made.

It is also a blog you can own. Signing in with Google gives you a blog of your
own, kept in **your own Google Drive** — not on a server here, because there
isn't one. Your posts are private until you press Publish, which shares one file
in your Drive so anyone with the link can read it without signing in to
anything. Unpublishing takes that back.

There are no comments, no analytics and no accounts other than Google's. The
[Privacy](#/privacy) page says exactly what that means.

The four posts above came with the repository as placeholders, to show the shape
of a post. Replace them with your own and this page along with them.
pages.title: About

pages.body:
Creating has no server of its own. It keeps nothing about you, because it has
nowhere to keep it.

**Signing in.** Signing in with Google lets this site make files in your own
Google Drive and open the files it made. That is the whole of the permission it
asks for. It cannot see, open or list anything else in your Drive, including
files another app made.

**Where your work lives.** Every post and every picture you add is saved in a
folder of your own Google Drive, under your own Google account. It is never
copied to a server belonging to this site, because there is no such server.
Nobody running this site can read it.

**What ever leaves your Drive.** Nothing, until you press Publish. Publishing
shares that one file, and the pictures it points at, so anyone with the link can
read them. Unpublishing takes the sharing away. Deleting a post deletes its
picture from your Drive too.

**What your browser keeps.** The site also keeps a copy of your work in your
browser, so it opens at once and works without a connection. Clearing this
site's data in your browser removes that copy and leaves the one in your Drive
alone.

**What is collected.** Nothing. There is no analytics, no advertising, no
tracking, and no account with anybody but Google.

**Taking it back.** Sign out whenever you like. To withdraw the site's
permission altogether, remove it at
[myaccount.google.com/permissions](https://myaccount.google.com/permissions).
Your files stay in your Drive, yours to keep or delete like any others.
pages.title: Privacy

pages.body:
Creating is free, and is offered as it is.

**What it is.** A place to keep the pictures you make — in your own Google
Drive — and to publish them as a blog if you want to.

**Your work is yours.** Nothing you write here is claimed by this site. It sits
in your Drive under your own account, and it stays yours whether you go on using
this site or not.

**Publish carefully.** Publish only what is yours to publish, and only what you
are happy for anyone holding the link to read. A published blog is readable by
anyone with the link until you unpublish it.

**No promises.** The site is provided without warranty of any kind, and it may
change or stop working without notice. Keep your own copy of anything you would
be sorry to lose.

**Ending it.** Stop using it whenever you like, and remove its permission at
[myaccount.google.com/permissions](https://myaccount.google.com/permissions).
pages.title: Terms

posts.body:
A circle, a square and a triangle, in that order, because that is the order they
were cut out in. The plan was one shape. The second one went next to it to see
whether two of them still looked like anything, and the third went in to fill the
gap the first two had left at the edge of the paper.

Flat colour, no outlines, and the same grey behind all three so nothing had to
fight for the front. The triangle is the pale one on purpose: it is the biggest,
and in blue it took over the whole page.
